title: The secret protocol of 23 August 1939 draws spheres of influence in the Baltic and in Poland
summary: The published secret protocol of 23 August 1939 divides German and Soviet spheres in the Baltic, including Lithuania.
body: The secret additional protocol, as Avalon prints it from the captured-document publication, says that in the Baltic states the northern boundary of Lithuania shall represent the boundary of the spheres of influence of Germany and the USSR, and it notes Lithuania's interest in Vilna. The card records this published English text. A Soviet archive original was not opened here. The wording on the page includes: "Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania), the northern boundary of Lithuania shall represent the boundary of the spheres of influence of Germany and the U.S.S.R. In this connection the interest of Lithuania in the Vilna area is recognized by each party. 2. In the event of a territorial and political rearrangement of the areas belonging to the Polish state the spheres of influence of Germany and the U.S.S.R. shall".

sources.title: Secret Additional Protocol, 23 August 1939

sources.note: Source is the Avalon text of the U.S. publication Nazi-Soviet Relations 1939-1941, not a Berlin or Moscow original inspected for this card.
